lessons.title: Preparing to plant cotton
lessons.html:
Preparing to plant cotton

Cotton is a warm-season crop. It needs warm soil to germinate, a long hot summer to grow, and no frost. In South Africa it is planted in spring to early summer, usually from about October to November, depending on the area and the rain. Your farm manager decides the planting date.

Soil and land

  • Cotton grows best in deep, well-drained soil.
  • The land is ploughed and prepared before planting, and fertiliser and lime are applied as the soil test shows.
  • Rows are marked or ridged at the spacing the farm uses.
  • The soil must be moist at planting. Plant after good rain or after irrigation.

Seed

  • Use certified seed of the cultivar the farm has chosen. Many cultivars are genetically modified to resist bollworm or herbicide; the farm will explain the rules for these.
  • Cotton seed is often treated with a fungicide or insecticide. It may be coloured to show this.
  • Keep seed bags dry, cool and away from animals.

Safety with treated seed

  • Treated seed is poisonous. Never eat it, never feed it to animals and never give it to anyone.
  • Wear gloves when handling treated seed, and follow the PPE on the seed bag label.
  • Do not eat, drink or smoke while planting. Wash your hands and face before eating.
  • Pick up any spilt seed so birds and animals do not eat it.
  • Empty seed bags must not be used for food or water; handle them as the farm instructs.

Tools

A hand planter (jab planter), a hoe, a measuring stick or marked string for spacing, and a container for seed. Check that tools are clean and working.

lessons.title: Planting the seed correctly
lessons.html:
Planting the seed correctly

Steps for hand planting

  1. Check the row. Follow the marked row or ridge so rows are straight.
  2. Space the holes. Use the measuring stick or marked string to keep the distance between planting spots the same, as your supervisor says.
  3. Make the hole with the hand planter or hoe at the right depth. Cotton seed must not be planted too deep; it is planted shallow, at the depth your supervisor gives you.
  4. Drop the seeds. Put the number of seeds per hole the farm instructs. Extra seedlings can be thinned out later.
  5. Cover the seed with fine, moist soil and press it lightly so the seed touches moist soil. Do not press too hard or make a crust.
  6. Move to the next spot and repeat.

Why depth matters

Too deepToo shallow
The seedling uses up its energy before reaching the surface and may dieSeed dries out, or birds eat it
Slow, uneven emergenceSeedlings fall over because roots are weak

After planting

  • Seedlings usually come up within some days if the soil is warm and moist.
  • Check the rows for gaps. Replant gaps quickly if instructed, so the stand is even.
  • When seedlings are established, thin them to the number of plants per spot or per metre the farm requires. Pull out the weakest ones and leave the strongest.
  • Keep the young crop free of weeds; cotton seedlings grow slowly at first and weeds can take over.
  • Watch for cutworms and other pests on the seedlings and report them.

Records

Record the field, date, cultivar, seed batch and amount used. These records help the farm trace problems and plan the next season.

Key points

  • Plant cotton in warm, moist soil in spring to early summer, on the date the farm sets.
  • Use certified seed; treated seed is poisonous, so wear gloves and wash hands.
  • Space holes evenly and plant shallow, at the depth given.
  • Cover with moist soil and press lightly.
  • Check for gaps, thin seedlings, control weeds and record the planting.

options.text: A warm-season crop that cannot take frost
A winter crop planted in June
A crop that likes cold, wet soil

What happens if cotton seed is planted too deep?

quiz.question: How do you keep the spacing between planting holes even?

options.text: Plant wherever the soil is soft
Use a measuring stick or marked string

quiz.question: When thinning seedlings, which ones do you remove?

options.text: Only the ones at the end of the row
